newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Colonial NZ details fund returns for Feb 1997.
newsitem.headline: Colonial NZ details fund returns for Feb 1997.

text.p: Colonial Investments New Zealand said on Thursday both New Zealand shares and bonds had lost ground over the February.
It made no asset allocation changes during the month in its Master Superannuation Scheme.
Colonial said the sharemarket had fallen 4.5 percent, dragged lower by Telecom, which fell 12 percent.
The Trade-Weighted Index hit new highs as the Australian dollar rose on the back of strong economic data.

Domestic interest rates rose following comments from U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan that the Fed may raise interest rates in a pre-emptive move before any sign of actual inflation became evident.

Greenspan also expressed concern that the U.S. sharemarket was being driven by "excessive optimism". New York's Dow Jones index passed 7,000 for the first time earlier in February, but fell after the remarks, to finish the month up just one percent.
Other major offshore markets were subdued.
New Zealand short rates rose to 7.75 percent at the end of February, while long term rates reached 7.65 percent.
The following table shows returns on Colonial NZ's managed and sector unit funds for February 1997 and for the 12 months to February.
Returns are expressed as a percentage and are net of tax.
Index returns for sector funds are those achieved by the relevant market index. Index returns for managed funds are those based on benchmark asset allocation.
